method.graphics: Software-WebGL fallback; no hardware FPS or audio enjoyment claim
method.interaction_limit: Discrete driver actions with Escape pauses; precision and reaction differ from continuous human mouse play.

attempts.account: Rushed past induction, found west receiver and recovered it. Reached Heart but held E at 3.3m outside activation range; died under crossfire before recovery.

Killed induction guard by aiming at optic, recovered west, learned cover and Heart receiver placement, recovered Heart and east. Reached return objective with 70 health/60 shield. Died during attempted sprint/dash return before reaching extraction zone.

ratings_scope: Whole-game impressions from two actual terminal attempts, not a certification. All cores reached; extraction finale and victory remain unverified. Ratings reflect witnessed experience and the coverage limits.

findings.finding: Cohesive rain-soaked industrial art direction, cyan objective lighting, bold title/end typography and concise memory archive create a clear identity.

Learning changed the run materially: precise induction optic fire earned a critical kill and preserved initial resources; second attempt collected all cores. Shield regeneration and recovery supplies made a damaged run recoverable.

Receiver interaction is easy to misjudge: at Heart, 3.3m and 3.2m distances showed MOVE CLOSER despite standing beside the large illuminated pylon and apparent floor ring. I spent exposed time holding E with no recovery. Brief does distinguish receiver from pylon, but geometry dominates the immediate view.

Threat readability competes with scenery and UI: small orange square enemies resembled mounted equipment to this new player; several RECENT FIRE/CHARGE panels and receiver labels accumulated near the weapon. I wasted shots and time identifying threats. This is an experience observation, not a damage or aim-system defect claim.

Return escalation was abrupt in this run: after all cores, a 4.5 second sprint/dash attempt from 70 health/60 shield ended in death. The guidance named beacon and cover aisles, but I did not resolve a safe return before dying. Cannot attribute cause to balance versus route/aim error without further attempts.
How to Play clearly lists controls but its long Threat Visor paragraph places substantial terminology into onboarding. In combat, interpreting merged sources and charges still required effort.
Presentation is polished for a browser slice; simple repeated architecture and enemy silhouettes, short observed mission arc, and unverified finale do not support AAA readiness certification.

driver_errors: One malformed JSON click and two selector errors while closing archive; corrected through visible UI. No gameplay state was forced.

closure.evidence: Driver closed result reported both exact PIDs and browserClosed:true; subsequent ps returned no rows.
